W2-06.fix: Call `store.create` directly. Delete `STORING`, the copy loop and `Taken`, and drop the `--N` handling.
W2-06.reasoning:
- `BackupStore::create` takes a per-router state lock and loops `write_exclusive` (hard-link, `AlreadyExists` means try the next sequence). It never replaces a backup, so the `STORING`/copy premise is false.
  - The page still probes with `store.get` on a `SystemTime::now()` second rather than the store's clock, holds a global lock, and refuses with `Taken` after 9 copies.
  - "Extra decryptions on every create" is slightly overstated: the usual first probe hits `NotFound` without decrypting. Decryption happens only on collisions.
  - Citations are off: `STORING` is at `store.rs:37`, `keep` at `170-200`.

W2-07.title: Read-only page views do far more work than needed
W2-07.rule: §4 "DON'T: Clone gratuitously / allocations"; §5 "yield in CPU-bound async"
W2-07.impact: Any user with Read can make the server decrypt up to 50 backups of up to 1 MiB each per page load. Large tables sort with O(n log n) allocations.
W2-07.fix: Take the size from file metadata (or record it in `BackupInfo`). Use `sort_by_cached_key`. Run the diff in `spawn_blocking`.
W2-07.correction: The decryption is off the async runtime (`spawn_blocking`). The real costs are needless decryption per page view, and a CPU-bound diff on the async worker (§5 "use `yield_now`/`spawn_blocking`").
W2-07.reasoning:
- `sizes` does decrypt every listed backup on the page (up to `PAGE_ROWS = 50`) just to measure it. It runs inside `spawn_blocking`, though, so it doesn't stall async workers; the cost is wasted CPU on the blocking pool for Read users.
  - The diff (bounded by `MAX_EDITS = 1000`) does run inline in the async handler.
  - The per-comparison lowercase allocation is real but trivial at table sizes.
  - The cited §4 "clone gratuitously" rule doesn't really fit decrypt-to-measure.

W3-03.title: Wi-Fi SSID, security, channel and country changes are never management-classified, but disabling the same access point is
W3-03.rule: project overlay Safety model (management changes run under fail-safe); focus item "correct planner called with correct risk".
W3-03.impact: kcc's host is on `WifiMaster0/AccessPoint0`, which the fake router classifies as management (see the `wifi.rs` test). Changing that access point's SSID or security to WPA3 drops kcc's link. No fail-safe timer is armed, so nothing rolls back.
W3-03.fix: Classify these planners with `detect_management` the same way `plan_up(false)` does. Then use `confirming_planned` on the `net_wifi_edit::field` POST (see W3-01).
W3-03.reasoning: `docs/SECURITY.md:201-204` states the design on purpose: "Interface description, SSID, radio/RF settings, MAC band/BSSID/VHT tuning and other non-address interface writes likewise remain ordinary Write and run without the recovery timer." The catalog test `ordinary_name_keyed_interface_leaves_remain_write` pins SSID and RF as Write, and encryption falls under "other non-address interface writes". W3-04.title: DHCP pool editor keeps only the first DNS server, cannot clear DNS, and lets a "new" pool overwrite an existing one
W3-04.rule: project rule (c) "Every curated write is read back and compared"; RUST_GUIDELINES §10 "Validate … input at system boundaries".
W3-04.impact:
- Editing only the lease of a pool with two DNS servers re-sends just `address1`, so the second server is lost (INFERRED: the router replaces both on a one-address `dns-server`).

  - "Add pool" with the name `_WEBADMIN` silently rewrites that pool's range, gateway and binding.
W3-04.fix: Carry every DNS server through the form (or two fields). Emit `no … dns-server` when the field is empty. In `save_pool`, refuse a name that is already taken when `existing` is absent, using `submit_reading` to check against `dhcp::read_pools`.
W3-04.reasoning:
- `PoolForm::of` keeps only `dns_servers.into_iter().next()`. `plan_pool` writes only `address1`, and only when there is one. An empty field produces `Vec::new()`, which sends no `no … dns-server` line.
  - `existing` affects only the title and the hidden inputs. `save_pool` never checks whether a new pool's name is already taken.
  - The catalog synopsis is `dns-server (address1 [address2] | disable)` with `multiple_input: false`, which supports the inferred loss of the second server.
  - Pool writes are also never read back (see NEW-1), so both silent cases report success.

W3-05.title: Failed router reads are swallowed into defaults that drive later changes

Submitting either unchanged plans a management change the user never meant. Elsewhere the user gets a misleading field error, and the audit records "gone" instead of "unreachable".
W3-05.fix: On a dialog `GET`, answer with `net_change::unusable(..)` (already used by `net_internet_settings.rs:46`). In checks, return `Rejected::Failed(unread(..))` instead of defaulting.
W3-05.correction:
1. The two dialogs whose wrong defaults could plan a management change still ask before it runs: security level uses `.confirming(Risk::Management)` (`net_interface_edits.rs:201`), and the address dialog uses `.confirming_planned` (`net_internet_address.rs:193`). The risk is a misleading preselected value, not a change made without confirmation.

W3-06.title: Three hand-written DomainError→WorkflowError mappings that already disagree

Two more copies live in `kcc-domain` (`dhcp.rs:245`, `clients/command.rs:204`), so a single shared mapping belongs below the web crate. W3-07.title: Tests of management changes send the confirmation up front, so a missing prompt cannot fail them
W3-07.impact: Both tests pass with W3-01 present and would still pass if the bracket were dropped from the prompt path.
W3-07.fix: Copy the firewall pattern: post with no fields, assert the prompt and that no command was sent, then post with `confirm=yes`.

W3-08.title: Firewall rule reorder builds its CLI line in the web layer, with a validated leaf that doesn't match the line

W3-09.rule: brief item 4 (defensive checks inside trusted code; string matching on error names).

W3-10.impact: Poisoned locks are silently ignored, and the create and delete closures are line-for-line twins that will drift.

W3-11.title: Same small helpers and constants duplicated across page families
W3-11.rule: brief item 4 (copy-paste, magic values repeated across files).

W3-12.title: Read-back regions assume permissions instead of computing them
W3-12.rule: overlay http-services (authorization reflected consistently); focus item "refresh regions consistent".
W3-12.impact: After creating a segment, a role (or firmware catalog) that allows `create` but not `delete` gets Delete buttons that answer 403. The page and its refresh show different controls.
W3-12.fix: Compute `Controls` in each read-back, as `net_interfaces::refreshed` and `policy_change::refreshed` already do.
W3-12.reasoning:
The claimed mismatch cannot happen:
  - Segment `create` and `delete` share permission `Write`, risk `Write` and catalog path `interface`. `Controls::allows` filters only on those, so `allows("create") == allows("delete")` for every role and firmware.
  - Route add and remove open the same operation (`family.operation()`).
  - NAT forward add and remove both use `"forward"`; NAT interface add and remove both use `"interface"`, the same key the full page passes to `allows`.
  - A read-back runs only after that operation was opened, which re-checks the permission. So the hard-coded `true` always equals what the page would compute.
  - What remains is an implicit coupling, not a bug.

W3-13.title: Static route read-back compares typed text with the router's stored text
W3-13.rule: project rule (c) (read-back compares values, not spellings).
W3-13.impact: Adding `2001:DB8:0::/48`, or `10.0.0.5` with mask 255.255.255.0, may be stored by the router in canonical form (`2001:db8::/48`, `10.0.0.0`). The route is applied but answered "VerificationFailed", and the duplicate check misses it too.
W3-13.fix: Canonicalise in `check` (parse into `Ipv4Addr`/`Ipv6Addr` and network-mask them) before building `StaticRoute`, or compare parsed addresses.
W3-13.reasoning: The typed `destination` and `gateway` text is stored as entered and compared with derived `PartialEq` against the router's stored words. Rust's `Ipv4Addr` parsing already rejects most non-canonical IPv4 spellings, but host bits (`10.0.0.5` with a /24 mask) and any IPv6 spelling (`prefix()` only parses) pass unchanged. The mismatch depends on the router canonicalising them, which is still INFERRED.

W3-14.title: Access-point rows round-trip through serde and read password presence from raw interface data
W3-14.rule: project rule (d) (secrets in secrecy types, never in Debug); RUST_GUIDELINES §4 (needless allocation).

W3-14.correction: The root cause is in `kcc_domain::interfaces::Interface`. The fix is a list reader for access points in `wifi`, plus stripping `authentication` from the domain `Interface` model.
W3-14.reasoning: The serde round trip and the presence check on `extra["authentication"]` exist as described. The Debug-printable copy of `authentication` is a property of the domain `Interface` model (`#[serde(flatten)] extra`) for every `show interface` read; this page neither logs nor renders it. W4-01.title: Explorer and console reads show stored secrets (ns3 blobs) to roles that lack `RevealSecrets`
W4-01.rule: project rule (d); overlay keenetic-control-center "(d) Secrets ... never reach ... tool results"
W4-01.impact: The built-in `viewer` role has only `Read`. It can open `/ui/r/home/explorer?path=show running-config` and press Run. It gets the router's full running configuration, including every `password ns3 …`, `wpa-psk ns3 …` and IPsec/PPP secret line. These are the same values the backup download strips for that role. The answer is also kept for download (`keep_response`). In the CLI console, a `RawRci` holder without `RevealSecrets` gets the same through `show running-config`. It also gets the startup config through `more flash:startup-config` (risk Write, so only `RawRci` is needed).
W4-01.fix: Run every explorer and console text answer through the same line redaction as `preview::stored`: `kcc_config` `parse` → `redact` → `ns3_redacted`. Alternatively, treat `show running-config`/`more` as needing `RevealSecrets`. Apply it in `Rendered::body`/`Rendered::text` whenever `reveal == false`, and add a test: a viewer runs `show running-config` and receives no `ns3` blob.
W4-01.reasoning:
- **Permission needed:** `/ui/r/{r}/explorer/execute` falls to `Permission::Read`. The handler then re-checks only `command_permissions(risk)`. `show running-config` is `CommandKind::Show`, so its risk is `Read`, so only `Read` is needed. The built-in `viewer` role holds exactly that.
  - **Path to the page:** a Read request goes `read_root`, then `answered`, then `Rendered::body(body, reveal)`. A `Text` body is passed through untouched. A JSON body is passed through `mask`, which matches member *names* only, so string lines such as `"... wpa-psk ns3 <blob>"` survive. A truncated answer is also kept for download.
  - **The blobs are real secrets:** `kcc_config::ns3::decode` turns an ns3 blob back into the plaintext secret.
  - **The code knows this:** `preview::stored` and `firewall::read` run running-config text through `redact`/`ns3_redacted` before anyone sees it. The explorer and CLI read paths do not.
  - **Remaining inference:** the exact shape of the real RCI answer is unknown (`docs/BACKLOG.md:18`). It does not matter here, because neither a text answer nor JSON string lines are masked.
  - **Second vector, no shape inference needed:** `mask` skips a secret-named member whose value is an object and recurses into it. In `"password":{"ns3":"<blob>"}`, the inner key `ns3` is not a secret name, so the blob is shown. The fake router's `show interface` projection returns exactly this shape (`projection/interface.rs:66-69`), so a viewer running `show interface` would see the blob.
  - **Console claims hold:** a `RawRci` holder without `RevealSecrets` gets the same leak through the CLI read path. `more` is an `Action`, so its risk is `Write` and only `RawRci` is needed.

W4-02.title: Any reader of a router can stop or follow other users' jobs, and job ids are predictable
W4-02.rule: http-services overlay (authorization per resource); BRIEF focus "background jobs (start/poll/stop ownership)"
W4-02.impact: A viewer starts one ping job, which reveals the process prefix. They then try nearby sequence numbers and timestamps against `POST /ui/r/home/system/jobs/{id}/cancel`. That stops an administrator's running diagnostic or explorer job, and they can stream its output. `JobRecord` has no owner field to stop this.
W4-02.fix: Store the starting username (or session key) next to the job id: in `keep_output` and in `JobFeeds::follow`. Require it to match in `explorer_job`, `followed`, both `cancel` handlers and both streams, or require an admin permission to act on other users' jobs.
W4-02.correction: This is a missing ownership check on read-only background jobs. A router-scoped viewer can cancel or watch other users' diagnostics and explorer read jobs, and the ids are easy to enumerate. Write jobs, raw jobs and the commit job are out of reach. The proposed fix (store the starting user, require a match or an admin permission) is sound.
W4-02.reasoning:
- **No ownership check exists.** `explorer_job` and `followed` filter only on router and kind, and `JobRecord` has no owner field. Stop needs router scope only, plus `RawRci` for `explorer.raw.*` jobs. Both streams need router scope only.
  - **Ids are predictable.** An id is unix seconds (`jobs.rs:407`), plus the process id and 4 bytes of entropy that stay constant for the process, plus a global counter. One job of your own reveals the constant parts. Starting two of your own jobs brackets the counter and time of everyone else's.
  - **A viewer can start jobs.** Diagnostics are `Risk::Read`/`Permission::Read`, so a viewer can start one and learn the id format.
  - **What a viewer can actually reach is narrow:**
    - Stop: other users' diagnostics and `explorer.read.*` jobs (for example `show log`). All of these only read.
    - Not stoppable by a viewer: `explorer.raw.*` jobs need `RawRci`, and the component commit is filtered out of cancel.
    - Follow: shows ping/traceroute lines or an answer rendered with `reveal=false`, which a viewer could produce by running the same tool.
  - **The cited rule is unsupported.** The http-services overlay has no per-resource authorization rule.

W4-03.title: Router-account protection fails open when kcc's login is empty or the profile lookup fails
W4-03.rule: RUST_GUIDELINES.md §2 "swallowed errors" (fail-closed); BRIEF anti-pattern "swallowed or downgraded errors"
W4-03.impact: For a token-auth router, `login == ""`. For any router, a registry read error makes it `""` too. Either way the "account kcc signs in with" guard never matches. A `ManageUsers` holder can then delete, or set a new password on, the router account kcc uses. kcc loses access after the bracket. A fail-safe timer may roll back only if the session dies before the disarm (INFERRED).
W4-03.fix: Make `profile_login` return `Result<String, _>`. Refuse the change (fail closed) when the lookup fails or the login is empty. For token profiles, record and compare the token's account.
W4-03.correction: For token profiles with an empty login, protection fails open on both Web and CLI. On Web, a registry read error also makes it fail open. Fix it at the source: refuse when the login is empty or unknown, and make `profile_login` return a `Result` that refuses on error.
W4-03.reasoning:
- **Fail-open is real.** `profile_login` turns a registry error into `None`, and callers use `unwrap_or_default()`, so the login becomes `""`. `plan_delete`/`plan_password` compare `name == ""`, which never matches.
  - **Token profiles may have an empty login.** `auth.rs:21` requires a login only when a password is used.
  - **Evidence is misattributed.** The set-password path is `secret_pages/user_password.rs:103-109` (and the dialog at `:79`, which also fails open). `user_forms.rs:103` is the Add path, which reaches `plan_password` only when a password is typed on Add.
  - **The token half is not Web-only.** The CLI compares against `profile.login` (`kcc/src/cli/domains.rs:147,173-179`), which is also `""` for a token profile. Only the lookup-error half is Web-specific.
  - **The lookup-error half is rare.** It needs the registry read to fail right after `Operation::open` loaded the same profile.
  - **Lockout is plausible but uncertain.** The change is `Risk::Management`, so a fail-safe or reboot bracket applies. Whether kcc's session can still disarm the timer after its own account is deleted is unverified.

W4-04.title: About 50 `pub(crate)` async handlers in scope lack cancel-safety annotations, including write paths
W4-04.rule: RUST_GUIDELINES.md §5 "Annotate every async fn with cancel safety" (1188)
W4-04.impact: `docs/BACKLOG.md:77` says "Ten non-public production async fns" lack the comment. This scope alone has about 50, several of which run management brackets. A future `select!`/timeout wrapper would get no warning.
W4-04.fix: Add `// NOT cancel-safe:`/`// cancel-safe:` to each one, and extend `cargo xtask cancel-safety` to `pub(crate)` items as the backlog item proposes.

Two of its listed items (`dns_vpn/flow.rs:212`, `dns_vpn/vpn_checks.rs:35`) are in this lane.

W4-05.title: Existence guards swallow read errors (one path lets "Add account" overwrite an existing account)
W4-05.impact: A transient read failure makes the name-taken check pass. "Add" then plans `user <existing>` plus tags and a password, which changes an existing account through the create dialog. In the other handlers, an unreachable router answers 404 "not found" instead of "unreachable", and the audit records `not_found`.
W4-05.fix: Propagate the read error to the kit's unreachable answer, as `vpn_import.rs:115-123` already does (`Err(error) => unread = Some(error)`).
W4-05.reasoning:
- `find` turns a read error into `None`, so the name-taken guard passes. `plan_account` then plans `user <existing>`, tags, and an optional password, with no existence check.

W4-06.title: Comments say management changes need `Destructive`; the code does not require it
W4-06.rule: BRIEF "comments that restate code or lie"
W4-06.impact: Reviewers and operators are told that management toggles are `Destructive`-gated, but per the owner decision they are not. The second `services.rs` tuple element is dead.
W4-06.fix: Correct the six comments. Collapse `switches` to one boolean, or keep both and say why.
W4-06.reasoning:
- `Risk` derives `Ord` in the order Read < Write < Management < Destructive. `SafetyNet::required` adds `Destructive` only when `risk >= Destructive`.
  - None of the cited files checks `Destructive` anywhere except in its doc comment.
  - The README ("`Destructive` is needed only for ...") matches the code, so the comments are stale.
  - The second element of the `switches` tuple in `services.rs:180-183` equals the first.

W4-07.title: Global caps evict other sessions' downloads and running jobs' answers
W4-07.impact: With 8 users making large reads, the oldest user's "download full answer" link returns 404 at once. If 32 explorer jobs start while a long `tools iperf3` runs, its completed answer is reported as "empty response".
W4-07.fix: Bound per session or user, not globally. Evict only finished jobs' slots, or keep the slot inside the job closure until a listener reads it.
W4-07.reasoning:
- Both bounded queues are global and evict the oldest entry no matter whose it is. `download` answers 404 when the entry is gone.
  - When a completed job's slot was evicted, `ending` shows `WEB_EXPLORER_EMPTY_RESPONSE`.
  - It is real, but needs 8 concurrent large-answer sessions or 32 explorer jobs during one long job, which is unlikely for this tool.

W4-08.title: The explorer offers Execute for background changes that it always refuses
W4-08.impact: A `RawRci` user sees an enabled button for `ussd send`, and every press is refused and audited as `validation_failed`.
W4-08.fix: In `detail`, apply the same `reads_only` predicate (make it `pub(super)`) and show a fourth `Runnable` state.

- `ussd send` is in the background list and has risk `Write`, and no domain registers it as a Read op, so `reads_only` is false and `build` always refuses it.

W4-09.title: Raw-form secrets are held in plain `String`s with derived `Debug`
W4-09.rule: project rule (d) "Secrets live in `secrecy`/`zeroize` types … never … `Debug` output"

W4-09.fix: Implement a manual `Debug` that omits `body`/`line`. Zeroize the `pairs`/`Bytes` copies, or move the text straight into `SecretString`/`SecretValue`, as `secret_pages::dialog::take` does.

W4-11.impact: A router that kcc reaches through `name.keenetic.pro` (with `allowed_suffixes`) loses its name after one unconfirmed click, and kcc is cut off with no fail-safe timer. Someone else can then book the name.

W4-13.title: Each log-page stream polls the router itself
W4-13.impact: Without a collector, N open log tabs across users make N `show log` reads every 5 s, which breaks the stated limit.
W4-13.fix: Share one poller per router (a `watch`/broadcast like `JobFeeds`), or document that the limit is per viewer.

W4-14.title: The RCI console's read batch sends the redacted projection
W4-14.impact: Today no Read command takes a registered secret, so nothing breaks. Any future such argument would be sent masked. The single-object path (`rci.rs:236-238`) sends the real value, so the two paths are inconsistent.

W5-01.title: An abandoned or timed-out Apply leaves the router claimed for the rest of the process's life
W5-01.rule: RUST_GUIDELINES.md §5 "Annotate every async fn with cancel safety" (1188), §6 "RAII Guards" (1290)
W5-01.impact: A user confirms Apply, and either the fresh read of a slow target takes more than 30 s or the user closes the tab. The future is dropped at an `.await`, so `release` never runs. The `active` entry (`wizard/service.rs:52-57`) keeps the target. Every other run of that wizard against that router then gets "busy" until kcc restarts. A related path: if `visit.save()` fails at `launch.rs:109` after the job started, `apply.rs:88` releases the claim while the job is running, and the record has no `run`, so the user cannot follow, commit or roll back.
W5-01.fix: Wrap the claim in a guard whose `Drop` releases it unless it is disarmed after `start_run` has been saved. Do the reads before claiming, and call `brackets::hold()` right before `Applier::start`.
W5-01.reasoning: The apply route sits under `brackets::budget` and the outer `brackets::own`. Neither apply handler, `launch`, nor `Prepared::new`/`Basis::of` calls `brackets::hold()`, so a 30 s budget timeout or a client disconnect drops the handler future at an `.await` after `claim`. Those awaits are `visit.analysis()`, `registry.client()`, `Basis::of` and the `JobRunner::start` locks. The only releases are in the `Err` arm, `settle`, `finish.rs:272` and `settle.rs:115`, and none of them runs in that case. The RCI read timeout is 30 s (`session.rs:54`), so one hung target read is enough to hit the budget first. `JobRunner::start` has no await after it spawns the job, so the job cannot start without its settler. One nuance: `claim` is keyed target→id and returns true for the same id, so the original run can retry, and a success or `Err` then releases. Every other run and user stays "busy" until that happens or kcc restarts. The save-failure side path is also real: `JobRunner`'s own `write_jobs` still blocks concurrent writes, but the record has no `run`.

W5-02.title: Fleet and dashboard SSE streams keep running after logout, user disable or role change
W5-02.impact: An admin narrows a role's router scope or disables a user. That user's open `/ui/sse/fleet` and `/ui/sse/r/{router}/traffic` streams keep pushing cards, live regions and traffic for routers no longer in scope, with no time limit.
W5-02.fix: Pass the session id and the store into `guarded`, and end the stream when `peek(id)` returns `None`. Check it on each event and on the keep-alive tick, or cap stream lifetime at the session idle timeout.
W5-02.correction: No guideline rule applies; this is a session-revocation gap. The root is the shared `overview::guarded` (`overview.rs:215`), so it also covers `system_pages/logs.rs:174`, `system_pages/jobs.rs:153`, `advanced/job_stream.rs:87` and `net_interface_traffic.rs:67`. The fix belongs in `guarded`.
W5-02.reasoning: Both stream handlers capture the role once. `guarded` only holds the `StreamPermit`, and nothing re-checks the session. `invalidate_user`/`invalidate_role` only edit the session map. So an open stream keeps rendering cards and live regions, with no lifetime cap beyond `KeepAlive`. The behaviour is real. The cited rule is not: overlay rule (e) is about CSP, CSRF and escaping, not session revocation.

W5-03.title: Migrations keep the whole sealed source config and the typed passwords forever
W5-03.rule: project rule (i) "retention limits apply to ... backups"; project rule (d)
W5-03.impact: Every migration ever started, including ones abandoned at step 1, keeps `source.sealed` (the full startup-config with every secret) and `passwords.sealed` on disk. That outlives backup retention and backup deletion. A copy run older than 24 h still works until someone opens `/ui/copy`.
W5-03.fix: Override `Finishing::discard` for the migration record (remove `Source` and `Passwords`). Check the age in `PresetRun::preset` for `Origin::Copy`. Add a retention sweep for run directories.
W5-03.correction: Also affected: runs of saved presets (`Origin::Preset`) abandoned before step 8 keep `passwords.sealed` forever, because `sweep` (`saved.rs:135`) expires only `Origin::Copy`. The fix stands: an override of `Finishing::discard` for migrations, plus an age-based sweep of every run's sealed parts.
W5-03.reasoning: Migrations use the default no-op `discard`. Nothing deletes `source.sealed` or `passwords.sealed` of a migration, and a restore seals a copy of a backup (`landing.rs:212-216`). That copy outlives the `keep_last`/`max_age` pruning. `PreparedRun::preset` opens a Copy transient without an age check; expiry happens only lazily in `sweep`. However, `docs/PRIVACY.md:24` already documents that only copy runs expire ("records and reports stay"). The files are also sealed under the backup key, so the extra exposure is old configurations surviving backup retention for someone who already holds the master key. The 24-hour Copy gap exposes only the owner's own copied settings.

W5-04.title: Changing source or target clears the password list but keeps `passwords.sealed`; old passwords are reused silently
W5-04.impact: A user types a new password for `alice` for target X, goes back and picks target Y. The preset page says no password is stored, yet an empty submit is accepted and X's password is applied on Y. In the migration wizard the review and plan for Y are classified with the stale password (`plan.rs:49,56`).
W5-04.fix: `store.discard(id, Sealed::Passwords)` wherever `forget_target_choices` runs (`choose_source` / `choose_target` in both wizards), or derive "stored" from one source only.
W5-04.correction: Limit the claim to the presets wizard (`presets_page/inputs.rs:94` vs `:139-145`). In the migration wizard the only inconsistency is that `record.passwords` is cleared while the sealed map, which the UI shows as stored, survives.
W5-04.reasoning: `forget_target_choices` clears `record.passwords`, but no caller discards the sealed file. The preset part is confirmed: the panel derives `stored` from the record (`inputs.rs:94`), so it says no password is stored, while submit accepts an empty field from the sealed map (`:145`). The migration part is not silent: its panel derives `stored` from the same sealed map (`migrate_wizard/inputs.rs:169,181`). That matches submit, so the old password is shown as kept, by design ("an empty field keeps one already typed"). The reused value is a password the same user typed for the same user name in the same run.

W5-05.title: Wizard file I/O, including fsync, runs on the async workers
W5-05.rule: RUST_GUIDELINES.md §5 "DON'T: Call blocking I/O in async functions" (1112)
W5-05.impact: On slow disks every wizard click blocks a tokio worker for one or more fsyncs. Listing gets slower as runs pile up (see W5-06), which stalls unrelated requests and SSE streams on that worker.
W5-05.fix: Make the `Store` methods async over `spawn_blocking`, or wrap them in a `spawn_blocking` helper.
W5-05.correction: none to the facts; the severity is lowered because the cost per request is bounded and small.
W5-05.reasoning: `Store` does synchronous `std::fs` reads and writes plus `sync_all` from async handlers. That is the §5 rule ("DON'T: Call blocking I/O in async functions"), and the crate otherwise uses `spawn_blocking` for similar stores. The `events.rs` load runs once, at stream end, not per event. Per request the cost is a few small-file fsyncs; the larger cost is the O(all runs) scan in `list`, which W5-06 already covers.

W5-06.title: Any Migrate user can create unlimited run directories, and every landing page reads them all
W5-06.impact: A scripted loop of POSTs fills the state disk or inodes. It also makes `/ui/migrate`, `/ui/copy` (which loads everything a second time in `sweep`) and the preset landing pages slower for every user, because each view reads every directory.
W5-06.fix: Cap open runs per owner, prune finished or abandoned runs past a retention window (this also fixes W5-03), and keep an owner index instead of scanning everything.
W5-06.reasoning: Each `POST /ui/migrate` or `/ui/copy` writes a new run directory, with no cap and no pruning. `Store::list` and `sweep` load every directory of every user. The route table requires `Migrate` (operator or above), and every start is audited, so this is an authenticated, attributable insider DoS or slow growth over time, not an anonymous one. It shares its fix with W5-03.

W5-07.title: The two wizards still duplicate apply, launch, target, inputs and download code after the engine split
W5-07.rule: BRIEF §4 "copy-paste duplication that drifts" (related KNOWN-BACKLOG "consolidation saved less than the line count suggests", which lists no specifics)
W5-07.impact: W5-01 has to be fixed twice, and the two copies already differ (the presets apply has a cancel-safety comment, the migration apply does not).
W5-07.fix: Move `apply` + `launch` + `settle` into `crate::wizard` behind a `Flow` hook for "record end". Move `attachment`, `fact`, the password check and `filters` into wizard or page_kit helpers, and the shared helpers out of `migrate_wizard`.
W5-07.correction: Use the line references above. This is maintainability, not a medium bug.
W5-07.reasoning: The duplication is real (apply, launch, settle, `attachment`, `fact`, the password loop, `filters`), and the comment drift is real: presets `apply` is marked NOT cancel-safe, the migration `apply` has no comment. Several citations are wrong. `migrate_wizard/preview.rs` has only 206 lines; `fact` is at 203-206 and the line-text closure at 131-144, not 474-477 or 402-415. `sse.rs` has a `lock` method, not the copied free function; `advanced.rs:175` and `system_pages/job_feed.rs:124` are additional copies. The only demonstrated cost is fixing W5-01 twice.

W5-08.title: Cross-crate reason keys and display text are matched as strings, and unknown keys fall into wildcard arms
W5-08.rule: RUST_GUIDELINES.md §3 "Use exhaustive match - avoid wildcard catch-all" (547); §7 "Overreliance on String" (1567)
W5-08.impact: A new or renamed reason in kcc-migrate makes a migrated setting read "unsupported", or drops a needed password or component from step 5, with no compile error.
W5-08.fix: Have kcc-migrate expose typed reason or input enums (`NeededInput::Install(name)`, `PasswordUser(name)`) and match them exhaustively.
W5-08.reasoning: Reason keys from kcc-migrate are matched as string literals, with `(None, _) => MIGRATE_REASON_UNSUPPORTED`. Components come from `strip_prefix("install ")` and users from the second word of `item.before`. A renamed reason in kcc-migrate silently changes the label or drops an input. §3 "Use exhaustive match" applies in spirit. There is no type to match on yet, so a typed enum is needed upstream.

W5-09.title: About 18 handlers and helpers have no cancel-safety comment
W5-09.rule: RUST_GUIDELINES.md §5 (1188) (related KNOWN-BACKLOG: `xtask cancel-safety` checks `pub` only; these items are not in its list)
W5-09.impact: The one handler where cancellation matters (W5-01) carries no warning.
W5-09.fix: Add the comments, and extend the xtask check to `pub(crate)` and `pub(super)`.
W5-09.reasoning: All 18 cited functions lack a `cancel-safe`/`NOT cancel-safe` comment, including the migration `apply`, which is the W5-01 path. They are not in BACKLOG:77's list of ten. The proposed xtask extension to `pub(crate)` and private functions is already BACKLOG:77, so only the new instances count.

W5-10.title: Errors are swallowed or recorded as the wrong outcome
W5-10.impact: A corrupt store file is logged in the audit trail as an authorization refusal. A preview is shown that the apply will always refuse. Users are told "busy" when the real failure is something else.
W5-10.fix: Map the I/O and crypto errors to `errors::internal` and record an audit outcome of `failed`.
W5-10.correction: Drop the `compose.rs` bullet and fix the preview line to `migrate_wizard/preview.rs:122`.
W5-10.reasoning: `reveal.rs:99-105` turns any `store.get` error (I/O, decrypt, a preset deleted between list and get) into an audited "forbidden" and a 403; confirmed. The preview's `passwords().unwrap_or_default()` (preview.rs:122, not 393) conflicts with apply's `Refused::Broken`. `Applier::start` maps `ApplyError::Job`, which includes job persist I/O, to "busy". The `compose.rs:147` bullet is practically unreachable, because the draft text was already read and parsed by `source_read::choose` before the draft was kept.

W5-11.title: A user-controlled form size makes review submit quadratic on the async worker
W5-11.impact: A crafted 1 MiB form against a large source can spend seconds of CPU per request on a tokio worker. The 30 s budget cannot preempt synchronous work.
W5-11.fix: Collect the form once into a `BTreeMap<&str, &str>` (last value wins) before the loop.
W5-11.reasoning: For each distinct `shown` index below `count`, `last()` does a reverse linear scan of the whole form, so the cost is O(distinct shown × pairs). It is bounded by the 1 MiB body and by `count`, which comes from the user's own 1 MiB source. A crafted form can burn seconds of CPU on a worker, which the budget cannot preempt. Only an authenticated Migrate user can reach it, so low is right.

W5-12.title: Up to 64 sessions are shared by all users; eviction drops a session another request is still using
W5-12.impact: User B touching 64 run ids evicts user A's sessions. A's cached analysis is lost, which means extra router reads. Worse, a request A has in flight keeps the old turn mutex while A's next request gets a new one, so the two can run interleaved and one save can overwrite the other.
W5-12.fix: Check the owner before creating a session, and skip evicting a session whose `turn` is locked (`try_lock`).
W5-12.reasoning: `Visit::open` calls `wizards.session(id)` (visit.rs:57, not 128) after `is_id` but before the owner check, so any well-formed id creates a session. At 64 sessions the oldest one with `live == None` is evicted, even while its `turn` is held by an in-flight request. The next request then gets a fresh mutex, which breaks the one-turn-per-run guarantee and allows a lost update.

W5-13.title: The copied preset is held in a plain `Vec<String>` that is never zeroized
W5-13.impact: WireGuard private keys and password hashes are copied into plain heap Strings and freed without being wiped, on both seal and open.
W5-13.fix: Serialize from borrowed `&str` straight into one `SecretString`, and deserialize into `Zeroizing<Vec<String>>`.
W5-13.correction: The rule (d) gap is in kcc-migrate's `Preset`/`PresetPayload` model; `saved.rs` only inherits it. Fix it there, or call it a model-wide deviation.
W5-13.reasoning: The Web transient does hold plain `Vec<String>` lines, but it mirrors the model. `Preset.lines` is a plain `Vec<CliLine>`, and kcc-migrate's own `PresetStore::save`/`open` serialize through a plain `lines` payload the same way. Changing only `saved.rs` to `Zeroizing` would not remove the plain copies, which live in `Preset` itself.

W5-14.title: Maps go through a JSON round-trip and silently become empty if it fails
W5-14.impact: If a future validating deserializer rejects one entry, the whole map is silently replaced with no renames and saved that way. It also costs an allocation per row.
W5-14.fix: `let mut map = M::default(); map.entries = pairs.map(MapEntry::new)...` (or a small trait for the three map types).
W5-14.reasoning: With today's derived `Deserialize` (`source: String`, `target: Option<String>`), `from_value` cannot fail for the JSON built here, so nothing is swallowed now. The round-trip is deliberate (comment at 263-264): the map types are `#[non_exhaustive]` and the function is generic over three of them. The proposed `M::default(); map.entries = …` needs a trait for a generic `M`. What remains is a hypothetical future failure and an allocation per row.

W5-15.title: Two stacked firmware-update caches with different retry rules, and a doc comment that describes the wrong one
W5-15.impact: Every dashboard poll for every viewer of a router whose check failed spawns a task (`fleet.rs:253`) that never asks the router. The comment misleads anyone maintaining it.
W5-15.fix: Keep one cache (the one in `ComponentsUpdateCheck`) and make `UpdateCache` a thin pass-through, or drop it.
W5-15.correction: Cite `fleet_updates.rs:117-144`. The impact is a misleading comment plus negligible spawns.
W5-15.reasoning: The two layers are confirmed. On `Failed`, the inner `ComponentsUpdateCheck` keeps `started` (`settle`, 136-144) and returns the cached status for the TTL. The outer layer resets `checked_at` on `Unknown`, so each status call for a router that never succeeded spawns a task that returns the cached value without asking the router. The comment at `fleet.rs:220-222` is half-true: it holds for `Skipped` (offline or not polled, inner `started = None`) but not for `Failed`. The cost is one trivial spawn per call.

W5-16.title: Migration passwords are mapped by row index; the hidden user-name field is ignored
W5-16.impact: If the server-side user list changes between render and submit (for example after a restart re-reads the target realm), a password is assigned to the wrong user. The hidden field is dead markup.
W5-16.fix: Key the password fields by user name, or check `user-N` against `needs.users()[N]`.
W5-16.reasoning: `user-N` is rendered and never read; passwords are bound by position in `needs.users()`. That list depends on `record.excluded()` and on the target analysis. A stale tab can post after another tab went back, changed the exclusions and returned to step 5, which passes the `Step::Inputs` check, and a password then lands on a different user. The presets inputs bind by index the same way.

W5-17.title: Test gaps: the cross-user check covers only GET, and tests assert on markup fragments
W5-17.impact: An ownership regression on a POST or SSE route would pass the suite. Template-only changes break unrelated tests.
W5-17.fix: Add one table-driven stranger test over every run route of both wizards. Assert on parsed elements or ids instead of markup. Move the router-form tests out of `dashboard.rs`.
W5-17.reasoning: The only stranger check on another account's migration run is a `GET` that answers 404. There is no stranger test for POST, `/events` or `/download` in either wizard; the presets "scoped" test covers presets, not runs. Every handler does go through `Visit::open` today, so this is a regression gap, not a live bug. The markup pins are real, at `records.rs:56,60` rather than 106-111.

X-01.title: CI and container workflows trigger on `main`, but the repository's branch is `master`
X-01.rule: RUST_GUIDELINES.md §12 "Required CI Tools" ("MUST run in CI on every PR. Failure blocks merge."), AGENTS.md G0/G1
X-01.impact: Pushes to `master` and pull requests against it, including Dependabot's, start neither CI nor the container e2e. No G0 or G1 gate (fmt, clippy, test, deny, audit, vet, machete, xtask gates, shellcheck, actionlint) blocks a merge. This also explains how X-02 could go unnoticed.
X-01.fix: Use `branches: [master]` in `ci.yml` and `container.yml`, or rename the default branch and update CONTRIBUTING.md. Then make the CI jobs required status checks.
X-01.correction: Medium, not high: the gap is in the CI process and has no runtime consequence. Fix it with `branches: [master]` in `ci.yml` and `container.yml`, or by removing the branch filter. Also fix `kcc.container:12` `blob/main`, which will 404.
X-01.reasoning:
The finding is correct. `ci.yml` and `container.yml` filter `push`/`pull_request` on `branches: [main]`, but the only branch is `master` and CONTRIBUTING.md says to branch from `master`. Once the repo is pushed with `master` as default, pushes, PRs and Dependabot PRs start no CI and nothing turns red, so the "Failure blocks merge" requirement in §12 fails silently. Several things limit the damage, though:
  - There is no remote, so nothing is published or bypassed today.
  - The `v*` tag triggers in `container.yml` and `release.yml` still fire.
  - Both workflows have `workflow_dispatch`.
  - G0 is a local gate in AGENTS.md.
  
  Nothing at runtime breaks and no product security control is defeated, so this does not reach "high".

X-02.title: The `gates` job cannot run `lint-completeness` as configured, and when it fails the other gates in that job are skipped
X-02.rule: RUST_GUIDELINES.md §9 "Keeping the profile complete"; overlay "Common alignment steps" ("the Cargo leg reads `lints.html` from the `rust-docs` component and fails when it cannot")
X-02.impact: The job installs 1.100.0 without `rust-docs` or `clippy`, so the Cargo leg exits 2. Because the job's steps run in sequence, `allow-gate`, `profile-eq`, `i18n-check`, `assets-check`, `cancel-safety`, shellcheck and actionlint never run. The Clippy leg also reads whatever `stable` the runner ships, not the pinned 1.100.0 used by the rustc leg. When stable becomes 1.101, the gate fails, or the wrong list passes, with no code change.
X-02.fix: Add `components: clippy, rust-docs` to the gates job, and replace `"stable"` with the active toolchain (for example `rustup run 1.100.0 clippy-driver`, or run `clippy-driver` from `rustc --print sysroot`). Move `lint-completeness` to the end of the job, or split it into its own job.
X-02.correction: Drop the "stable" sub-claim as mandated by the vendored script. What remains is that `components: rust-docs` (and `clippy` if it should not depend on the runner's stable) is missing from the gates job, and the job fails deterministically and visibly.
X-02.reasoning: The core claim holds. The `gates` job installs 1.100.0 with the minimal profile, sets it as default, and adds no `rust-docs`. `rustc --print sysroot` then points at a sysroot without `share/doc/rust/html/cargo/reference/lints.html`, so `cargo_lints::run` returns `GateError::Read`. The step fails and the later steps in the job (`allow-gate` … actionlint) never run. The sub-claim about `rustup run stable` is not a repository defect: it copies the vendored core script verbatim (`rustup run stable clippy-driver -W help`, guideline line 2015), which the overlay says xtask mirrors. The failure is also loud and fail-closed (a red job on the first run), not a silent pass.

X-03.title: e2e step functions ignore `set -e`, so failures in the middle of a step pass
X-03.rule: project rule (g) (live suites must prove the behaviour); RUST_GUIDELINES.md §13 (tests that cannot fail)
X-03.impact: Bash ignores errexit inside a function called as an `if` condition. I confirmed this with a scratch run: `f(){ false; echo after; true; }; if f; then echo PASS; fi` prints PASS. The container e2e is the only proof that the seccomp profile allows the write and save path. If the profile misses a syscall that only `config save` uses, the step still passes. The `no-denials` grep does not catch it either, because kcc reports such failures as "RCI transport failed" (deploy/podman/README.md says so). A broken profile would then ship. The live "one reversible write" proves nothing.
X-03.fix: In both `step()` helpers, run `set +e; ( set -e; "$@" ) >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?; set -e`, then test `rc`. I verified this form returns 1 on a failure in the middle of the function.
X-03.reasoning: `step` runs each function as an `if` condition, where bash suspends `errexit` for the whole function body. In `domain_write_save`, failures of `set-description`, `static-host` and `config save` are masked by the last command, `config state`, which does not check them. In `sighup_reload`, the `wait_line` result is ignored and only `healthz` decides. `live-e2e.sh` `reversible_write` passes when `clients register` fails, because the final check only proves absence. `web_login_dashboard`'s mid-function `[[ -n "${csrf}" ]]` is also ignored, though later checks catch it. README:172-178 explicitly relies on the functional steps, not the log grep, to prove the profile, so this weakens the only seccomp proof.

X-04.title: Releases and published images skip every G1 gate
X-04.impact: Pushing a `v*` tag on any commit, including one that never went through CI (see X-01), publishes a GitHub release and `ghcr.io/...:<tag>` plus `:latest` with no advisory, license or test check. A RUSTSEC advisory published after the last merge is not caught at release time.
X-04.fix: Expose `ci.yml` through `workflow_call` and add a `gates` job to `release.yml` and `container.yml` that the build and push jobs `need`. At minimum, run `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` there.
X-04.correction: Low. The fix is unchanged: a `cargo deny check` plus `cargo audit` job that the build/push jobs `need`.
X-04.reasoning: Correct as stated: neither workflow runs or `needs` deny, audit, vet, test or clippy before publishing. However, G1 is documented as a gate the contributor runs before release, not as something CI enforces. A tag push needs repository write access. The container push does wait for the full container e2e. The real cost is a missed advisory or an unreviewed commit at release time, which is a process gap rather than a weakened runtime control.

X-05.title: No gate checks lint *levels* against the vendored profile
X-05.rule: RUST_GUIDELINES.md §9 Policy, "Every crate uses the profile below, unchanged" and "No group-level `allow` in any manifest" (line ~1632-1645)
X-05.impact: Setting `unwrap_used = "allow"`, or `pedantic = "allow"`, in both `Cargo.toml` and `xtask/Cargo.toml` passes `lint-completeness`, `profile-eq` and clippy. The overlay's claim that the profile is "verbatim" is not enforced. Today the tables are identical to §9; I diffed them.
X-05.fix: In `lint-completeness`, require every entry to be `deny` or `forbid`, except `redundant_pub_crate = "allow"`. Alternatively, extract the TOML block from the checksummed `RUST_GUIDELINES.md` and run `profile_eq::compare` against root.
X-05.correction: This is hardening, not a defect: nothing violates it today and the core asks for no such check. Optional fix: compare the root tables against the TOML block extracted from the checksummed `RUST_GUIDELINES.md`.
X-05.reasoning: I normalised comments and whitespace and diffed the tables myself. The root tables equal the §9 profile line for line (only the markdown fence differs). The xtask tables are equal apart from `[lints.x]` versus `[workspace.lints.x]`, which is the single-package form §9 allows. The gate is indeed names-only and `profile-eq` compares xtask to root only. But the core's own completeness procedure is names-only too (`grep -oE '^[a-z0-9_]+' Cargo.toml`, line 2018), and the core mandates no level check. Nothing is violated today, and a level change would be a visible manifest diff.

X-06.title: The cargo-vet gate is nominal, and the documented bump procedure keeps it that way
X-06.rule: RUST_GUIDELINES.md §10 "DO: Use `cargo vet` for supply chain trust" (line ~3033)
X-06.impact: Regenerating exemptions on every bump exempts the new version automatically. A compromised patch release of `rmcp-server-kit` that clears the 3-day cooldown would pass `cargo vet` once the bump commit follows the documented procedure.
X-06.fix: On bumps, require `cargo vet` to pass through imports or `cargo vet certify`/`diff`, and stop regenerating exemptions in bump commits. Audit the direct security-critical crates first.
X-06.reasoning: Every first-party trust decision is an exemption. The CI comment makes "regenerate exemptions" the standing bump procedure, so a new version of `rmcp-server-kit`, `rustls` or `reqwest` is exempted automatically and `cargo vet` can never fail on a bump. §10's purpose ("someone actually read this dependency's source code") is not met. The cooldown and deny/audit remain.

X-07.title: The xtask workspace's dependencies are never advisory- or vet-checked
X-07.rule: RUST_GUIDELINES.md §12 "Required CI Tools" (`cargo audit` on every PR)
X-07.impact: Code from 128 crates runs in the CI gates job and on developer machines, and a RUSTSEC advisory in any of them goes unreported. The missing deny config for xtask is already in BACKLOG; audit and vet are not.
X-07.fix: Add `cargo audit -f xtask/Cargo.lock` to the `xtask` job.
X-07.correction: "never advisory-checked" is false. What remains is that xtask has no `cargo vet` coverage.
X-07.reasoning: The advisory half is wrong. The `xtask` CI job runs `cargo deny --manifest-path xtask/Cargo.toml check`, and `check` includes the `advisories` check (the root `deny.toml` `[advisories]` is the config it picks up; BACKLOG:78 confirms that config is being read). RUSTSEC advisories in xtask's lockfile are therefore reported. Only `cargo vet` does not cover the xtask workspace, and that is developer and CI tooling, not shipped code.

X-08.title: `ci.yml` checkouts keep the token in `.git/config`
X-08.rule: overlay http-services / workflow least privilege (inconsistent with this repository's own `container.yml` and `release.yml`)
X-08.impact: Jobs that compile third-party `build.rs` and proc-macros (clippy, test, rustdoc, msrv, gates) leave `GITHUB_TOKEN` readable in `.git/config`. The scope is `contents: read`, so impact is limited.
X-08.fix: Add `with: { persist-credentials: false }` to every checkout in `ci.yml`.
X-08.correction: This is a consistency fix with no demonstrated consequence.
X-08.reasoning: Accurate: none of the `ci.yml` checkouts set `persist-credentials: false`. But the token is `contents: read`, the workflow uploads no artifacts (the "artipacked" path), and code that can read `.git/config` (`build.rs`, proc-macros) already has the full checkout. The token adds next to nothing.

X-09.title: Image publishing: prerelease tags overwrite `:latest`, and the version label is always 0.1.0
X-09.impact: Tagging `v0.2.0-rc.1` moves every Quadlet or `run.sh` deployment on `:latest` to the release candidate on its next pull. Every image claims `org.opencontainers.image.version=0.1.0`.
X-09.fix: Push `:latest` only when `TAG` has no `-`, and pass `--build-arg VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"`.
X-09.reasoning: Every `v*` tag, including `v0.2.0-rc.1`, is pushed as `:latest`, and `run.sh` and the Quadlet unit default to `:latest`. `VERSION` is never passed to `podman build`, so the label is always `0.1.0`.

X-10.title: `web-smoke.sh` puts the admin Web password on a command line
X-10.rule: project rule (d) (secrets never exposed); local-user trust boundary
X-10.impact: While the live run is in progress, another local user can read the password from `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` or `podman inspect`. They can then log in as `admin` to the kcc on 127.0.0.1, which holds the live router's credentials and has write permission.
X-10.fix: Export `WEB_PASSWORD` in the environment and pass `-e WEB_PASSWORD` without a value, or use `--env-file` on a 0600 file.
X-10.reasoning: The per-run admin password for `smoke` goes into the `podman run` argv, which other local users can read via `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` (absent `hidepid`) while the run lasts. With it they can log in to the loopback kcc that holds live router credentials. One sub-claim is wrong: `podman inspect` is not a cross-user vector, because rootless containers are per-user.

X-11.title: kcc-rci depends directly on the outdated getrandom 0.2, and the duplicate-skip reason does not mention it
X-11.rule: RUST_GUIDELINES.md §10 "Configure `cargo deny`" (each `skip` names the chain that forces it); §11 Supply Chain (latest versions)
X-11.impact: If `ring` leaves the tree, the 0.2 duplicate stays, and the skip still claims ring forces it. First-party code stays on an unmaintained API (`getrandom::getrandom`, `crates/kcc-rci/src/auth_ndw4.rs:88`).
X-11.fix: Use the workspace `rand` 0.10, or getrandom 0.4 (`getrandom::fill`), in kcc-rci, and keep the skip reason accurate.
X-11.correction: The skip reason is not wrong. Optionally move `kcc-rci` (`auth_ndw4.rs:88` and `auth_digest.rs:188`) to `getrandom` 0.4 / `rand` and add `kcc-rci` to the reason while 0.2 remains.
X-11.reasoning: `ring` really does pull in `getrandom 0.2.17`, so the skip reason is accurate today. The "if ring leaves" impact is hypothetical. The only concrete point is that first-party `kcc-rci` uses the old major at two call sites while 0.4 is already in the tree.

X-12.title: `ci-local.sh` has drifted from `ci.yml`
X-12.rule: none (the script says "Keep this file in step with ci.yml")
X-12.impact: A contributor gets "all green" locally while CI's cancel-safety gate fails.
X-12.reasoning: The script says it is kept in step with `ci.yml`, but its `gates` step lacks `cargo xtask cancel-safety`, which CI runs at line 191.

X-13.title: Seccomp drift never blocks, and the profile admits 32-bit ABIs the image never uses
X-13.impact: The profile can grow beyond what the binary needs without anyone being told. A post-compromise attacker can use the compat-ABI syscall entry points. The default Docker profile does the same.
X-13.fix: Optionally make the drift check blocking on amd64, and keep only `X86_64` and `AARCH64`.
X-13.reasoning: The drift check is `continue-on-error: true`, and the profile lists X86, X32 and ARM next to the two shipped architectures. The README documents both as deliberate, and the generator already fails on any syscall with no group. Nothing to fix urgently.

T-01.title: Secret-leak tests cannot fail for JSON, `Debug` or `?`-formatted traces: each secret contains `"` (and `\`)
T-01.rule: project rule (d); RUST_GUIDELINES.md §13 "Use mutation testing to verify test effectiveness" (3518)
T-01.impact:
- `Debug` and JSON both write `"` as `\"` and `\` as `\\`. The raw secret is therefore never a substring of those encodings.
  - Example: a regression that copied the plaintext into the audit entry's `detail` would produce `...with \"quote\" and \\\\ slash` in `audit.jsonl`, and every assertion above would still pass. The same holds for a `#[derive(Debug)]` on a secret-holding type or a `?`-formatted tracing field.
  - The suites that guard rule (d) only catch leaks printed raw through `Display`.
  - A smaller gap (INFERRED): `TraceCapture` is installed with the thread-local `set_default` (`kcc-domain/tests/support/mod.rs:83`). The audit writer works inside `spawn_blocking` (`kcc-app/src/audit/writer.rs:53`), so events from that thread are not captured.
T-01.fix: Check each sink against every encoding the secret can take there: `serde_json::to_string(secret)` without its outer quotes, `secret.escape_debug()`, and the CLI-quoted form. Alternatively, add a second secret with no characters that need escaping and run the checks on both.
T-01.correction: Scope note: "only catch leaks printed raw" is overstated. `kcc/tests/cli_domain_writes/secrets.rs` (`PASSWORD = "s3cret-Vpn-Passw0rd"`, WireGuard keys) and `kcc-migrate/tests/support/apply_secrets.rs` use quote-free secrets against the audit log. The `kcc-app` scrub test and the four domain suites listed are vacuous.
T-01.reasoning: The secret markers are `"a secret with \"quote\" and \\ slash"`, `"…with spaces \"quotes\""`, `"wireless passphrase with \"quotes\""`, `"ppp password with \"quotes\""` and `"vpn fixture with \"quote\""`. Each is checked with `!output.contains(secret)` against `{:?}`, `serde_json::to_string`, `audit.jsonl` (JSON) and `{:?}` of `request_log()`. All of these escape `"`, so the assertions cannot fail. The worst case is `secrets_write.rs`: it deliberately passes the plaintext as `json!({"detail":secret})` to test the scrub at `workflow.rs:390`. If the scrub broke, the audit line would hold the JSON-escaped secret and the test would still pass. It is even broader than reported: `quoting.rs:23` always double-quotes and escapes `"`/`\` on the wire, so the raw-text `running_config_text()` and `request_log` checks are vacuous too. The `set_default`/`spawn_blocking` sub-point is plausible and remains INFERRED.

T-02.title: `live_presets` and `live_mcp` cannot reach a real router; their twins hide it with `allow_loopback`
T-02.impact:
- With the live variables set against, say, 192.168.1.1, both suites pass the gate and the serial check: `capture::connect` uses `OutboundPolicy::default()`, which allows private networks.
  - The `kcc` process (`live_presets`) and the MCP registry (`live_mcp`) then refuse the router, so both suites always fail on hardware.
  - The twins pass because loopback is allowed, so the fake runs never exercise the real outbound path. The live campaign cannot produce `live_presets` or `live_mcp` evidence.
T-02.fix: Copy `outbound` from the admitted `KCC_LIVE_TARGET_CONFIG` into the hermetic `kcc.toml` and into the MCP registry, as `live_domains/campaign.rs:157-161` and `live_migration/rehearsal.rs:211-215` already do. In the twins, set `allowed_networks` instead of relying on loopback alone.
T-02.reasoning: `OutboundPolicy::default()` allows RFC1918 addresses, but `RouterRegistry::new` replaces them with `with_allowed_networks` built from an empty `OutboundConfig`. `allows()` then admits only loopback (when enabled), configured networks, or global addresses with a matching suffix. The `kcc` child (`live_presets`) and the MCP registry (`live_mcp`) therefore refuse `192.168.x.x`, after `admit`/`capture::connect` (default policy) has already passed. The loopback twins hide this, while `live_domains` and `live_migration` already pass `admission.outbound`.

T-03.title: Fake router request log keeps only the last parse line of a batch and can misattribute lines under concurrency
T-03.rule: overlay `http-services.md`: none; BEHAVIOUR.md says the log "records ... non-secret root parser lines" (lines 242-246)
T-03.impact:
- A two-line change `[a, b]` appears in `request_log()` as `b` only. A secret line in a batch also overwrites the previous item's line with `None`.
  - Two overlapping requests (A records, B records, A's body arrives) put A's line on B's record, and B then overwrites it.
  - Absence assertions built on this log can pass wrongly. Examples: "never saved" (`live_domains/harness.rs:153-158`), "never disarmed" (`harness.rs:183-186`), "nothing sent" in the bracket matrices.
  - Order and presence assertions with concurrent posts (`kcc-web/tests/explorer_pages/bracket_budget.rs:225-228`) can flake.
T-03.fix: Record parse lines per request, not at `last_mut()`. Carry a record index in a request extension set by the middleware, and store `Vec<Option<String>>` of lines per record. Document batch behaviour in BEHAVIOUR.md.
T-03.correction: This is a fidelity bug in the fake that could mask future absence assertions. No current test is demonstrated to be wrong.
T-03.reasoning: The batch collapse is real. `record_request` pushes one record per HTTP request, and `post_one` calls `record_command` for each array item on `last_mut()`, so a `[a, b]` batch logs only `b`, and a secret last item blanks it. That contradicts BEHAVIOUR.md ("non-secret root parser lines"). However, no current assertion is shown to pass wrongly. The arm/disarm lines are single-line requests (`any(line == ARM)`, `last() == DISARM`), and "the suite saved" is also checked through `startup_config_text` equality. The concurrency interleaving remains INFERRED.

T-04.title: The fake hashes or encodes plaintext secrets itself, so "kcc hashes / never stores plaintext" tests check the fake; the conversion is undocumented
T-04.rule: §13 "Mocks must preserve the behavior being asserted"; brief item "fake router behaviour that diverges ... without being marked assumed"
T-04.impact:
- These tests pass whether kcc sends plaintext or not; the "hashes" and "never in running config" properties are the fake's.
  - A config that has been through the fake carries a `password md5` that does not authenticate on the fake, so migration tests cannot cover password replay.
  - A related gap: the request-log secret filter (`server.rs:440-449`) has no marker for `crypto ike key <name> <psk>`. A plaintext IKE PSK therefore stays in `request_log()`, contrary to BEHAVIOUR.md lines 242-244.
T-04.fix: Mark the plain→md5 and plaintext→NS3 conversions **assumed** in BEHAVIOUR.md. In the tests, assert on what kcc sent (the parse line before the fake's conversion), not on the stored text. Add `"ike key"` to the request-log secret markers.
T-04.correction: Drop "tests check the fake, not kcc" as a defect. Keep these items: the undocumented conversions, the md5-versus-HA1 inconsistency, and the missing `ike key` marker.
T-04.reasoning:
The headline is weak. kcc is supposed to send `password plain` and plaintext `wpa-psk` (the router hashes or encodes them), and `secrets_write.rs` labels these assertions "fake must store a hash" and "fake must encode the PSK". So no kcc property is mis-attributed. The sub-points are real:
  - The plain-to-md5 and wpa-psk-to-NS3 conversions are not marked assumed in BEHAVIOUR.md, which CONTRIBUTING requires.
  - The stored `md5(password)` disagrees with the realm HA1 that both the fake's auth (`server.rs:726`) and the project's own live probe (`probe.rs:76`, `ndw2::ha1` as `password md5`) use. `password md5 <x>` also never updates the fake's auth, so password replay can't be covered.
  - `crypto ike key <name> <psk>` matches none of the request-log secret markers, contradicting BEHAVIOUR.md:242-244.

T-05.title: Live migration reads a live source router without the serial allowlist
T-05.rule: AGENTS.md "Every live test reads the serial via `show identification` and refuses any router not listed"; project rule (g)
T-05.impact: `KCC_LIVE_SOURCE_URL` can name any router, typically the production one, and the suite downloads its full startup config with secrets without checking its serial against `KCC_LIVE_ALLOW_SERIAL`. The owner's "refuse any router not listed" guarantee does not hold for the source.
T-05.fix: Call `connect` plus `verify_serial(&client, &live.allowed)` on the source before `registry.create`, and return a `Refusal::SerialNotAllowed` for it.
T-05.correction: This is a contract violation on a read-only path the operator opts into explicitly, so low rather than medium. The fix is unchanged.
T-05.reasoning:
Correct: the `SourceInput::Live` router is registered and its startup config downloaded with no `verify_serial`, which contradicts AGENTS.md's "Every live test reads the serial … and refuses any router not listed". It is mitigated in three ways:
  - The access is read-only.
  - The operator has to explicitly supply `KCC_LIVE_SOURCE_URL` and its admin password file.
  - The source registry uses the admitted target's `outbound` policy, so it must sit inside the test config's `allowed_networks`.
  
  The default source is a file.

T-06.title: `live_mcp_smoke` skips silently: no tracing subscriber, so `live-skip:` is never printed
T-06.rule: AGENTS.md "A missing variable makes the live test log `live-skip:<reason>` through `tracing` ... It never passes silently."
T-06.impact: `cargo test -p kcc-mcp --test live_mcp -- --ignored` without the variables reports `ok` and nothing names the skip. `KCC_LIVE_ALLOW_WRITE=1` without `KCC_LIVE_TARGET_CONFIG` also drops to read-only with no message (`live_mcp.rs:59-70`).
T-06.fix: Add `drop(tracing_subscriber::fmt().with_writer(io::stderr).try_init());` as the first line, and warn when writes are requested without a config.
T-06.reasoning: With no subscriber installed, `tracing::warn!("live-skip:…")` goes nowhere. It is not completely silent, because `live_matrix::record_skip` writes a skip row to the evidence file. `write_config: config.filter(|_| write)` drops writes silently, but the matrix then says "reads only".

T-07.title: Ports reserved by bind-0-then-drop are reused by child processes
T-07.rule: §13 test tiers / determinism; brief item "ports ... that collide in parallel runs"
T-07.impact:
- The listener is closed before `kcc serve` binds, so a parallel test or a fake router can take the port in between.
  - Two reservations in a row can even return the same port. `metrics_serve` then has `listen_port == metrics.bind`, and the child fails to bind.
  - In `cli/health.rs` the healthcheck can answer 0 against another test's server (a false pass).
T-07.fix: Have `kcc serve` accept `listen_port = 0` and log the bound address, then parse it from the "listening" line. Alternatively, pass an inherited, already-bound socket.
T-07.reasoning: The bind-to-0, read port, drop listener, pass to child pattern is a real TOCTOU in parallel test runs. The frequency is kernel-dependent (INFERRED), and the false-pass case in `health.rs` needs another kcc on the reused port.

T-08.title: Read-only live suites contact routers without a `test_device = true` profile
T-08.rule: project rule (g) "Live suites run only against router profiles marked `test_device = true`"
T-08.impact: Only the serial allowlist stands between these suites and a production router. They still log in as admin and download its full configuration. Rule (g) has no read-only exception.
T-08.fix: Require `KCC_LIVE_TARGET_CONFIG` with `test_device = true` for every live suite, and keep the serial check as the second gate. If read-only runs on non-test devices are intended, record that as an owner decision in the project overlay.
T-08.reasoning: Rule (g) and AGENTS.md state the restriction with no read-only exception, and these suites log in as admin and read `running-config` with only the serial allowlist as a guard. It is not listed as an owner decision.

T-09.title: Live migration probe writes after the safety net and records results instead of asserting them
T-09.rule: brief item "tests that print 'evidence' instead of asserting"; project rule (g)
T-09.impact:
- The probe account is created with no fail-safe timer armed. A `?` failure between the create and `no user` leaves it on the router's running config.
  - The target-realm control (`results[1]`) is never asserted. A probe that always fails (wrong tag, outbound refusal) records `false/false` and the suite passes.
T-09.fix: Run the probe inside an armed fail-safe timer, or before the rollback, and remove the account on every path. Assert that `target_realm_hash_accepted == Some(true)` before trusting the source-realm result.
T-09.correction: Drop the `live_campaign_matrix` sub-claim and keep the probe ordering, cleanup and missing control assertion.
T-09.reasoning: The probe runs after `applier.rollback()`/`commit()`, with no timer armed. A `?` failure between `password md5` and `no user` leaves a readonly-tagged account in running config (unsaved, so a reboot clears it). `results[1]`, the target-realm control, is recorded and never asserted, so a probe that always fails yields an uninformative pass. The `matrix.rs` sub-claim is wrong: `campaign()` is a skip-row recorder by design, not a behaviour test.

T-10.title: Bracket fate matrices are copied across the Web, MCP and domain tests
T-10.impact: Changing an arm or disarm line or adding a fate means editing three tables in step. A row fixed in one surface silently drifts in the others.
T-10.fix: Keep the full fate matrix in `kcc-domain`. Have each surface test one row per fate to its code and message, from a shared table in `kcc-testkit` or test support.
T-10.correction: Move the arm/disarm lines and fault constructors into `kcc-testkit`. The per-surface rows are justified.
T-10.reasoning: The duplication is real: `edges()` is copied verbatim in Web and MCP, `lines()` is the same in the domain tests, and the batch table is identical. But each surface asserts its own mapping (Web message keys versus MCP codes such as `management_outcome_unknown_fail_safe_armed`), which already is the "one row per fate per surface" the fix proposes. Only the copied arm/disarm constants and fault rows carry drift risk.

T-11.title: Source-grep tests stand in for behaviour tests
T-11.impact:
- A formatting or naming change breaks the first test. `use std::process::{self as p}; p::Command::new` is still caught, but `use std::process::Command as Run; Run::new(..)` or `std::os::unix::process::CommandExt` are not.
  - Both tests check the text, not the property: that the process runs with privileges dropped and never spawns.
T-11.fix: Test the privilege floor through the binary (run as a uid that should be refused, check exit code 77). Express the subprocess ban as a `clippy::disallowed_methods`/`disallowed_types` entry for `std::process::Command`.
T-11.correction: Bypass example: `use std::process::{Command as Run}`. Exit-code coverage of the privilege floor exists outside this test.
T-11.reasoning: The cited bypass is wrong: `use std::process::Command as Run;` contains `std::process::Command` and is caught. A real bypass is `use std::process::{Command as Run}; Run::new(..)`. Exit 77 is already tested through the real binary (container CI `--user 0`, the e2e `privilege-floor` step and the unit tests), so the first-statement grep only adds an ordering check. The substring ban remains weaker than a `clippy::disallowed_types` entry.

T-12.title: `Debug` strings compared as an equality proxy
T-12.rule: RUST_GUIDELINES.md §13 "DON'T: Assert on `Debug` output as a stable format" (3538)
T-12.impact: Both sides use one toolchain, so it does not break on upgrades. But a field that `Debug` skips or redacts would be compared as equal.
T-12.fix: Derive `PartialEq` for `TableQuery` in tests, or compare its fields.
T-12.reasoning: Both sides are `{:?}` of the same type, so §13's instability concern (comparing against a literal rendering) does not apply. Equality-through-Debug is still a weak proxy, and `TableQuery` has no `PartialEq`.
